21	    year: 2025

28	      intensional structural reward for neurosymbolic formalization.

34	    title: "DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models"

38	    category: neurosymbolic-rl
39	    role: method-component

43	      baselines from group scores.

58	      formalization, though Logic-RL uses extensional (answer-correctness)
59	      rewards rather than STA's intensional structural rewards.

165	    title: "Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF"

167	    year: 2025

173	      rapid-then-convergent growth. STA's ISR follows these principles

177	      initial growth with gradual convergence. PAR method achieves 5%+
178	      win rate improvement on AlpacaEval 2.0.

181	    title: "Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs"

184	    venue: "arXiv 2506.14245"
185	    category: reward-shaping
186	    role: background

189	      reasoning. STA argues that for neurosymbolic formalization, binary reward
190	      is insufficient and structural reward is needed to avoid reward hacking.

192	      RLVR with binary verification implicitly teaches correct reasoning
193	      strategies, not just answer matching.

196	    title: "Rubric-Grounded Reinforcement Learning: Structured Judge Rewards for Generalizable Reasoning"

200	    category: reward-shaping

211	    title: "On Designing Effective RL Reward at Training Time for LLM Reasoning"
212	    authors: "Jiaxuan Gao, Shusheng Xu, Wenjie Ye, Weilin Liu, Chuyi He, Wei Fu, Zhiyu Mei, Guangju Wang, Yi Wu"
213	    year: 2024
214	    venue: "arXiv 2410.15115"
215	    category: reward-shaping
216	    role: background
217	    relevance: >
218	      Demonstrates that learned process/outcome reward models can hurt RL
219	      training, producing worse performance than simple success reward only.
220	      Directly explains plan005 NEGATIVE: STA's ISR as auxiliary process
221	      reward degrades prove_rate compared to exec-only baseline.

228	    title: "Beyond Correctness: Harmonizing Process and Outcome Rewards through RL Training"
229	    authors: "Chenlu Ye, Zhou Yu, Ziji Zhang, Hao Chen, Narayanan Sadagopan, Jing Huang, Tong Zhang, Anurag Beniwal"
230	    year: 2025
231	    venue: "arXiv 2509.03403"
232	    category: reward-shaping
233	    role: background
234	    relevance: >
235	      Shows that naively combining PRM+ORM signals leads to performance
236	      degradation. PROF consistency filter retains only PRM-ORM consistent
237	      samples, achieving 4%+ improvement over blending. Suggests STA should
238	      only apply ISR when consistent with execution outcome.

240	      Process rewards frequently suffer from inaccuracies and reward hacking
241	      susceptibility. PROF filters training data by PRM-ORM consistency,
242	      outperforming naive reward blending by 4%+ accuracy.

252	      First study on overoptimization in composite reward models. Shows that
253	      fixed-weight linear scalarization of component rewards leads to
254	      degradation past a threshold. Proposes constrained RL with dynamic

257	      Correlation between component RMs significantly affects overoptimization
258	      thresholds. Constrained RL with Lagrange multipliers outperforms

262	    title: "Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking"
263	    authors: "Joar Skalse, Nikolaus H. R. Howe, Dmitrii Krasheninnikov, David Krueger"
264	    year: 2022
265	    venue: "arXiv 2209.13085 / NeurIPS 2022"
266	    category: reward-shaping
267	    role: background
268	    relevance: >
269	      Formal proof that for stochastic policies, two reward functions are
270	      unhackable only if one is constant. Theoretically explains why any
271	      non-zero ISR weight can decrease prove_rate -- this is a fundamental
272	      property of reward composition, not STA-specific.

# Literature Map for Solver Trace Ablation (STA)
# Categories:
#   1. neurosymbolic-rl: Neurosymbolic reasoning + RL/GRPO
#   2. reward-shaping: Reward shaping for code/formal verification
#   3. mutation-testing: Mutation testing in software engineering
#   4. intensional-analysis: Intensional program analysis
#   5. reward-hacking: Reward hacking / overoptimization
#   6. fol-formalization: FOL/Prolog formalization with LLMs
#   7. goodhart-overoptimization: Goodhart's Law theory and dose-response dynamics
#   8. verification-reward: Solver/prover as RL reward signal

papers:

  # ============================================================
  # Category 1: Neurosymbolic reasoning + RL/GRPO
  # ============================================================

  - id: deepseek-r1
    title: "DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning"
    authors: "DeepSeek-AI"
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv 2501.12948 / Nature 2025"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: method-component
    relevance: >
      Demonstrates that pure RL (GRPO) can incentivize reasoning in LLMs without SFT.
      STA builds on the same GRPO framework but replaces binary outcome reward with
      intensional structural reward for neurosymbolic formalization.
    key_finding: >
      DeepSeek-R1-Zero trained via GRPO alone achieves 71% on AIME 2024,
      showing emergent chain-of-thought reasoning from RL alone.

  - id: deepseekmath
    title: "DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models"
    authors: "Zhihong Shao, Peiyi Wang, Qihao Zhu, Runxin Xu, et al."
    year: 2024
    venue: "arXiv 2402.03300"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: method-component
    relevance: >
      Introduces GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization), the RL algorithm
      used in STA training. GRPO eliminates the critic model by estimating
      baselines from group scores.
    key_finding: >
      GRPO matches PPO performance while significantly reducing training
      resources; improves GSM8K 82.9->88.2% and MATH 46.8->51.7%.

  - id: logic-rl
    title: "Logic-RL: Unleashing LLM Reasoning with Rule-Based Reinforcement Learning"
    authors: "Xian et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv 2502.14768"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: direct-competitor
    relevance: >
      Uses rule-based RL (REINFORCE++) for LLM logical reasoning on synthetic
      logic puzzles. Closest competitor to STA's approach of RL for logical
      formalization, though Logic-RL uses extensional (answer-correctness)
      rewards rather than STA's intensional structural rewards.
    key_finding: >
      REINFORCE++ outperforms GRPO on logic puzzles with superior stability;
      rule-based reward design is critical for RL-based logical reasoning.

  - id: mellgren-prolog-grpo
    title: "Training Language Models to Use Prolog as a Tool"
    authors: "Niklas Mellgren"
    year: 2024
    venue: "arXiv 2512.07407"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: direct-competitor
    relevance: >
      Uses GRPO to train a 3B LLM to generate Prolog code for reasoning,
      directly comparable to STA's approach of GRPO-training a formalizer.
      Key difference: uses pass/fail reward vs STA's structural ISR.
    key_finding: >
      GRPO is effective for teaching small LLMs to use Prolog as a tool
      for logical and mathematical reasoning.

  - id: satlm
    title: "SatLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models Using Declarative Prompting"
    authors: "Xi Ye et al."
    year: 2023
    venue: "NeurIPS 2023"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: background
    relevance: >
      Neurosymbolic approach where LLM generates declarative specifications
      verified by SAT solver. Similar pipeline to STA (LLM->formal spec->solver)
      but uses prompting, not RL training.
    key_finding: >
      Declarative formulation outperforms imperative program-aided LMs by 23%
      on GSM; achieves SoTA on LSAT and BoardgameQA.

  - id: deepproblog
    title: "Neural Probabilistic Logic Programming in DeepProbLog"
    authors: "Robin Manhaeve, Sebastijan Dumančić, Angelika Kimmig, Thomas Demeester, Luc De Raedt"
    year: 2021
    venue: "Artificial Intelligence 298"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: background
    relevance: >
      Foundational neural-probabilistic logic programming framework that integrates
      deep learning with ProbLog via neural predicates. Establishes the intellectual
      tradition of combining neural networks with logic programming that STA extends
      to LLM-generated Prolog with RL training.
    key_finding: >
      End-to-end differentiable framework integrating neural perception with
      probabilistic logical reasoning; supports program induction and learning
      from examples.

  - id: neurasp
    title: "NeurASP: Embracing Neural Networks into Answer Set Programming"
    authors: "Zhun Yang, Adam Ishay, Joohyung Lee"
    year: 2020
    venue: "IJCAI 2020"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: background
    relevance: >
      Integrates neural networks with answer set programming (ASP), using
      ASP rules to constrain and improve neural network training. Complementary
      to DeepProbLog; together they represent the neuro-symbolic LP foundation
      that STA's LLM-to-Prolog pipeline builds upon.
    key_finding: >
      ASP semantic constraints improve neural network perception accuracy;
      demonstrates bidirectional benefit of neural-symbolic integration.

  - id: thought-like-pro
    title: "Thought-Like-Pro: Enhancing Reasoning of Large Language Models through Self-Driven Prolog-based Chain-of-Thought"
    authors: "Xiaoyu Tan, Yongxin Deng, Xihe Qiu, Weidi Xu, Chao Qu, Wei Chu, Yinghui Xu, Yuan Qi"
    year: 2024
    venue: "arXiv 2407.14562"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: direct-competitor
    relevance: >
      Uses Prolog engine to generate verified reasoning trajectories, then trains
      LLMs via imitation learning to replicate them. Directly comparable pipeline
      to STA (Prolog verification + LLM training), but uses imitation learning
      instead of GRPO with structural reward.
    key_finding: >
      Prolog-verified reasoning trajectories as training signal improve LLM
      logical reasoning; self-driven framework enables LLMs to formulate
      rules from instructions and leverage Prolog for derivation.

  # ============================================================
  # Category 2: Reward shaping for code/formal verification
  # ============================================================

  - id: lightman-verify-step
    title: "Let's Verify Step by Step"
    authors: "Hunter Lightman, Vineet Kosaraju, Yura Burda, et al."
    year: 2023
    venue: "arXiv 2305.20050 / ICLR 2024"
    category: reward-shaping
    role: method-component
    relevance: >
      Establishes that process supervision (step-level reward) outperforms
      outcome supervision (final-answer reward) for reasoning. STA's ISR
      is analogous: it provides structural process-level signal about which
      components of a formalization matter, rather than just pass/fail.
    key_finding: >
      Process-supervised reward model achieves 78% on MATH, significantly
      outperforming outcome-supervised models. Released PRM800K dataset.

  - id: reward-shaping-rlhf
    title: "Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF"
